chapter: Cass Carr, Crawley, Burnet and Cootie Williams
title: Richard Fulbright, Edmond Hall and Cookie Mason of the Ross band
summary: Holmes remembers Fulbright as a fine bassist, Hall as downtown-oriented, and Cookie Mason as a trumpeter he took for a gambler; touring bands faced jam sessions.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Now, other members of that Ross De Luxe Syncopator Band that came here, one who was at the time playing bass in the band was Richard Fulbright.
Fulbright, yeah.
What can you tell me about Fulbright?
Well, Fulbright was a bass player, and a damn good one, too. I mean, he was one of the best. He
Holmes (11/29) - 5
really was. But it's one of them things. Some get the breaks, some don't. You know what I mean?
Right. Now, he was the kind of bass player that could play both tuba and the string bass?

Yeah, he played everything. He was very good. Uncle Dick, yeah. There's nothing more I can say about him. Just a good bass player, and some of them get breaks... He worked with quite a few bands. I can't remember whose bands he worked with...
Bingie Madison, I think.
It could have been.
Edmond Hall came in with that Ross De Luxe Syncopated Band, too.

Well, see, Hall, he... I don't know what happened to him when they first got here, because I didn't meet him until later. I think he was kind of implanted with the Dixieland boys downtown. You know, I think. Of course, I mean, he was giggin' around up there, too. You'd take a gig wherever you could get 'em. They were hard times. But I think he hung around with the Dixieland boys more than uptown.
Then there was another trumpet player, Robert "Cookie" Mason.
Well, there's nothing I could say too much
Holmes (11/29) - 6

about Cookie, because I didn't know until years later that Cookie was even in a... I didn't know Cookie was a musician. I had been knowin' him for years and didn't know he was a musician. But at the time I met Cookie, I think he was a chauffeur for some big man downtown. He had a chauffeur's job. Every time I saw Cookie, he was all dressed up like he was a rich man or something. I didn't know he was even a musician.

Yeah, he would always be around the club... Oh, I actually thought he was a big-time gambler. Because he was around the Rhythm Club, where they gambled. Most of the time they had a big game goin' in there. And he would always be around, and I figured he was just another gambler hangin' around. Because he was dressed up all the time. He was very neat, you know.
But he was a good trumpet player, too. I've worked a few gigs with him. A very good trumpet player.
Yeah, they had good trumpet players in that band.
Yeah, you mentioned that when these bands would come into town, that they would...
At the jam sessions.
And cutting contests.
And cutting contests, yeah. And those that could show some promise, they could stay, and the ones that
Holmes (11/29) - 7
couldn't, they had to get out of town. They didn't hang around.
